## Says

- "I make candles. Whatever anyone tells you, I make candles."
- "The back benches have something to say. They always do."
- "Bastian, sit down. No, the other kind of sitting down."
- "A Caller rules nobody. Some days I wish I could rule the stew queue."
- "Three pages from the capital this fortnight. The queen disagrees with me beautifully."

??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Evening, *Player*. If you have come to ask the leader of Urbanograd for something, I am afraid there is no such person. There is a chandler who chairs the arguments. Will that do?
    - *Player*, the letter-carrier! The queen answered, you know. Four pages. She says I am wrong about the guilds and right about the patrols, and she wants the recipe for Mags's stew. I will not be sending it; Mags would never forgive either of us.
    - Listen to that. Bastian has been on his feet for an hour and has so far argued both sides of the door twice. Go and hear him, then Quint, and then come and find me. I will be here. I am always here on Table nights.
    - The Table agreed in a single night. I am still not over it. Dimity has checked the shelves, and she says it is the fastest yes in forty years. Now we wait on Hex and a very old lock.
    - The iron door is open and Leland stands by it like he was born there. Keeper of the Low Door: the Table chose him before I had finished saying his name. Second fast decision this year. People will start to talk.
    - Leland's chalk map is pinned up beside my chair now, all four levels of it. I read his tallies out at the Table: who went down, what they put back down. Your name comes up a lot, *Player*. Bastian has started cheering it.
    - Perch sent a pigeon to say you would be bringing me something from the Rooftops. Starling's dates and Perch's list, both? Good. I want them in my hand before I write a word to the capital.
    - The dates and the list went east with my last letter, every line of them. No answer yet. The queen answers everything, eventually, usually with an argument. This time I am hoping for an answer instead.
    - What can a candle-maker do for you?
        - *Choice:* What does a Caller do?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the Open Table.
        - *Choice:* You write to the queen?
        - *Choice:* What worries the Table these days?
        - *Choice:* What became of the door under the hall?
        - *Choice:* What will the queen make of Starling's dates?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Convene the Table. Keep order, which mostly means keeping Bastian to under an hour. And make sure the quiet ones get a turn, because the loud ones will take every turn there is if nobody stops them.
    - It does not mean ruling anybody. People ask me to rule on things every day, and every day I say no and hand them a candle. This is my first year as Caller and I have said loudly that it will be my last. Nobody believes me.
    - Anyone who lives in Urbanograd may stand up at the Open Table and speak. Anyone. A hundred years of it: lamp-oil taxes, roof repairs, whether a goat may attend. The goat may, by the way. Carried.
    - It is loud and slow and it runs till dawn, and Mags feeds everybody, and Dimity writes it all down, jokes included. I sat under those benches as a child and thought it was better than any play. I still do.
    - Every fortnight for nine years. I wrote her an angry letter once, about the Guard's patrols stopping short of our road. I expected nothing. She wrote back herself, three pages, agreeing with half and arguing with the rest. The patrols were extended the next year.
    - We argue about everything now: guilds, theatre, whether a kingdom needs a crown. She concedes a point the moment it is fairly made, which nobody at the Table has ever done except Bastian, and he does it by accident.
    - Fewer food carts every season. Brindle asking for volunteers because the monsters come closer to the walls than they used to. Moth counting the names in the hat. Mags's pot fed from rooftop tubs.
    - And the Table was built to be slow. Slow is good for most things. I am afraid of the day something will not wait for us to finish arguing.
    - Still shut. The Table said yes; the lock has not yet heard. Hex is the one to talk to, on Workshops Row. Bring patience. Bring a riddle, if you have one; Hex likes to trade.
    - Open, and Leland keeps it, with a rope and a lamp and a map in chalk on the kitchen wall. If you want to go down, ask him. If you come back up with stories, tell me. I will read them at the Table.
    - Honestly? I do not know. Starling's flickers, Perch's refused routes, some dates matching and some not. I laid them side by side on my table for a whole night and could make nothing of them that I would put my name to.
    - So I sent them as they are, with no theory attached. The queen has better eyes and more of them. Some of the dusk routes are open again, Perch tells me. Not all of them. I am grateful for some.
    - Mind the stew queue on the way out. And come to the Table some night. Sit at the back. I will make sure you get a turn.
